summary: 10.0.34.18 Enterprise Release - Server Root Cause Remediation for Import Loaders & Full 8-Loader Server Contract Parity (PostgreSQL party_code UNIQUE constraint conflict resolution, Sales customer.id contract, Purchases supplier.id & invoiceDate contract, Bank Statement bankAccount & row fingerprint contract, and Item Master remarks & HSN requirements)
highlights: 1. Server Root Cause Analysis & Resolution for Customer Import 500 Error: Diagnosed underlying cause of 'The ERP server could not complete this operation' (HTTP 500) as PostgreSQL duplicate key constraint violation on party_master(party_code). Resolved by proactively checking server-level party existence, pre-loading both CUSTOMER and SUPPLIER records, correctly routing existing records to PUT /api/master/parties with valid id and rowVersion, and handling conflict recovery.

2. Comprehensive 8-Loader Server Contract Verification: Full audit across all 8 import loaders (Item Master, Customers, Suppliers, Sales, Purchases, Categories & Lookups, Purchase Recon, and Bank Statement) directly against Spring Boot controllers, services, repositories, and entity models.

3. Sales Import Server Contract Alignment: Resolved customer object requirement (customer.id) expected by OperationDtos.SaleDto, and enforced source: 'IMPORT' so server preserves imported invoice numbers instead of auto-generating new ones.

4. Purchases Import Server Contract Alignment: Resolved supplier object requirement (supplier.id) expected by OperationDtos.PurchaseDto, mapped bill date to invoiceDate, and mapped vendor bill number to referenceNo.

5. Bank Statement Import Server Contract Alignment: Resolved BankReconciliationDtos.ImportRequest field mismatch by sending bankAccount (previously accountNumber), sourceRowNumber, and transactionFingerprint, ensuring debit/credit parity and preventing server rejection.
6. Master Categories & Values Lookups Parity: Synchronized lookups cache checks against both lookupCode and lookupValue to align with server validateLookup constraints.
